title: Willis Young's playing, last meeting in 1930 and later union job
summary: Phillips says Willis Young could not play as well as Lester but praised Phillips's power; he last saw him in Montana in 1930, and Young later held an important union post in Los Angeles and died in 1943.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Willis Young couldn't play as good as Lester Young, though.

Oh, no! Hell, no. Shit, he couldn't gooder than me! That's why he liked me so well. He said, "You blow just like Joe Oliver and Louis Armstrong" -- I'd never met them, you know. He said, "You got a lot of power." He said, "They have power. Now, if you was in New Orleans on one of them parades, they would like you, because you blow loud and strong." I said, "Thank you." I didn't know what he was talking about. He'd always take me everywhere he'd go; he
Phillips - 194
wanted me to go with him.
When did you last see Willis Young?
The last time I saw him was 1930.
So you'd been in Bronson's band at that time.
No< I hadn't been in Bronson's band.
Well, you joined Bronson in '28, right?
Oh yeah. I had been in there, that's right.
So what occasion did you see Willis Young? He lived until 1943, right??
Yeah, that's when he died, in '43.
Where was he living when he died?
In Los Angeles.
Anyway, what was going on when you last saw him? What was he doing?
Seems to me I saw him somewhere when I went out there with... Oh yeah. We ran across him with Bronson's band, that's what it was, up in Montana -- somewhere up in there.
Was he still touring?
Yeah, he had that show.
How long did he keep touring?
Oh, he kept touring until he quit. Then he got to be an executive in the union.
When did he quit?
Phillips - 195

Must have been about '40. During the War. Yeah, '41. Because Lester said he wasn't involved with show business no more. He had a big job. He was a very intelligent man. He had a big job in the Musicians Union out there.
Yeah, out there with Paul Howard.
Yeah, Paul Howard. He used to have a band, didn't he.
Right. But he was a big man in the union out there.
I know, yeah.
That's interesting. That was quite a story about that jam session up there.
Yeah.
